result:
I found and fixed the bug, and added regression tests. `npm test` passes: 9 of 9.

**Root cause:** in `src/payments/gateway/payload.js`, `buildChargePayload` turned the invoice currency into the gateway's lower-case form (`"JPY"` → `"jpy"`) and then passed that lower-case code to `toMinor`. The currency list in `src/lib/currency/registry.js` only has upper-case codes, so `"jpy"` wasn't found. The code then silently used the default of 2 decimal places, so ¥1,500 was sent to the gateway as 150,000. The PDF was correct because invoice totals are worked out with the upper-case code. USD and EUR are fine only because their real decimal count happens to equal that default.

**Fix:**
1. **`src/payments/gateway/payload.js`**: the amount is now converted using the invoice's own upper-case currency code. The lower-case code is still sent as the gateway's `currency` field.
2. **`src/lib/currency/registry.js`**: the decimal-count lookup now upper-cases the code first. Refunds, payouts, coupons, late fees and proration all use the same conversion helper, so a lower-case code from any of them could otherwise cause the same error.

**Regression tests** (`test/charge.test.js`): JPY 1500 → 1500 and KRW 25000 → 25000, both with the lower-case gateway code. A third test covers BHD 1.234 → 1234 (3 decimal places). I ran the tests against the old code and all three fail there.

The same bug also hit 3-decimal currencies (BHD, KWD), but in the other direction: those customers were charged 10 times too little. The other zero-decimal currencies in the registry (VND, CLP) were overcharged ×100 like Japan and Korea. You may want to find and fix past charges in all four of those currencies, as well as JPY and KRW.
